  Carrow Point's signature, the light's own name spelled out in fire.

  At dawn, the coast guard found the trawler (B[0m[3mMargaret Anne(B[0m anchored safely in the lee of Gull
  Island. Her captain said he had lost his instruments in the storm and was steering blind toward
  the rocks when he saw it: three seconds of light, seven of darkness. He said he had known exactly
  where he was.

  The automated system was installed in April, as scheduled. Elias packed his logbooks into two
  cardboard boxes and moved to a cottage in the village with a window facing the point.

  Every night, he still watches the light turn. Three seconds on, seven dark. The machine keeps
  perfect time.

  Sometimes, though, he swears it hesitates on the dark beat. It's never more than a heartbeat, as
  if the lighthouse is holding its breath, waiting for footsteps on the stairs.
